H.2.name: JAM.Erasure.encodeWith
H.2.note: split is not materialised: word p of chunk j is read in place as `word data (2 * k * j + 2 * p)`

H.3.name: JAM.Erasure.encodeWith
H.3.note: join^#: the result's chunk i joins word i of every piece (`wordOctets`); `JAM.Erasure.recover` joins the same way

H.4.name: JAM.Erasure.encodeWith
H.4.note: transposition is done by indexing: piece p takes word p of every chunk, and the result's chunk i takes word i of every piece

H.6.name: JAM.Erasure.recover
H.6.note: that recovery inverts encoding is proved with Mathlib in the separate package `proofs/ErasureProofs`, which the book cannot import

H.8.name: JAM.Erasure.GF.mul
H.8.note: elements are naturals below 2^16 in the polynomial basis; the modulus is `JAM.Erasure.GF.poly`, addition is `JAM.Erasure.GF.add` (XOR)

H.10.name: JAM.Erasure.encodeWeights
H.10.note: the target indices g(0), …, g(v − 1) are exactly I

H.11.name: JAM.Erasure.codeIndex
H.11.note: computes the inverse of f (the code index validator j receives); f itself is not built

H.13.name: JAM.Erasure.encodeWith
H.13.at: if j < d then word data (2 * k * j + 2 * p) else 0
H.13.note: p is never built: its values at the code indices are interpolated from these d′ points (`JAM.Erasure.lagrange`, `JAM.Erasure.interpolate`)
